# Requirements

Rex is Sidiora Labs' framework for building complex, high-quality web application interfaces that AI agents can write and that AI agents can operate. One declaration per capability, one folder convention per page, one checker that fails the build when anyone steps outside them.

## Requirement 1: Declarative primitives with one canonical shape

**User Story:** As an agent writing a Rex app, I want each capability declared once in one known shape so that I never choose between patterns.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. entity(), action(), page(), policy() and flow() each accept exactly one declaration object whose shape is exported as a TypeScript type and validated at declaration time; a malformed declaration throws with the field name.
2. Every declaration carries a stable string id derived from its name; two declarations with the same id in one app throw at registry build time.
3. Declarations contain no React imports and are importable from both server and client bundles.

## Requirement 2: Action projections

**User Story:** As an agent, I want one Action declaration to produce every surface it needs so that no route, hook, palette entry or audit record is written by hand.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Each Action becomes one oRPC procedure with input and output validation from its schemas; the procedure name equals the action id.
2. Each Action is callable from the client through a typed act() hook that returns a TanStack mutation, invalidates the queries the action declares, and records the result in the outcome region.
3. Each Action with a label appears in the command palette; each Action with a shortcut is bound to that key combination while its page is active.
4. Each Action is invocable by URL: <page route>?act=<action id>&input=<json>; invalid input renders a validation outcome, it does not throw.
5. Each Action invocation on the server writes one audit record with actor, action id, input digest, outcome, effect class and timestamp.
6. Each Action with effect irreversible requires a confirmation step before the handler runs on all four invocation routes.

## Requirement 3: Page folder convention

**User Story:** As an agent, I want the files of a page to be discoverable by name so that the folder tree is the component tree.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A page directory contains page.ts, view.tsx, states.tsx and optionally hooks/, regions/<name>/region.tsx, regions/<name>/parts/*.tsx, overlays/*.tsx and test/; the Vite plugin resolves these by convention without barrels.
2. Every region named in page.ts regions has a regions/<name>/region.tsx file, and every regions/<name> folder is named in page.ts; the checker reports either mismatch.
3. Every overlay named in page.ts overlays has an overlays/<Name>.tsx file, and every overlays file is named in page.ts.
4. Part files are PascalCase components with a single default export; hook files are camelCase starting with use and export a single function.
5. A part shared by two pages is moved to app/components by rex promote; the checker reports a part imported from another page's folder.

## Requirement 4: Required data states

**User Story:** As a user or agent, I want every page to render a sensible screen in every data state so that nothing is blank or spinning forever.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The RexDataState type is the closed set loading, empty, stale, partial, offline, permission-denied, recoverable-error, terminal-error, ready.
2. states.tsx must export a component named for every state the page declares in page.ts states (default: all nine); a missing export is a type error and a checker error.
3. The runtime resolves the current state from the page's queries, policy result and connectivity, renders the matching export, and writes the state into the sidecar.
4. The ready export is view.tsx; the other eight receive the page params and a retry function.

## Requirement 5: Import boundaries

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want layering enforced by the checker so that models cannot drift the architecture.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The checker enforces the import table in [design] import_table for page.ts, view.tsx, region.tsx, parts, hooks, overlays and states.tsx.
2. No file under app/pages/<a> imports from app/pages/<b> where a differs from b.
3. No component file calls fetch, the oRPC client or a store adapter directly; data flows through hooks in hooks/ or app/data.
4. Each violation is reported with file, line, rule id, the offending import and the allowed alternatives.

## Requirement 6: Derived shell and typed navigation

**User Story:** As an agent, I want routes, header, nav and back behaviour to come from page declarations so that no shell switch is hand-written.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The router is built from every page.ts route and params schema; unknown routes render the app-level not-found state.
2. Header title, back target and nav visibility are read from page.ts chrome; the shell has no per-page switch statements.
3. nav.to(page, params) is typed against the manifest; passing params that fail the target page's schema is a compile error and a runtime validation outcome.
4. Page params and draft state live in the URL as declared by page.ts draft; a reload restores the same screen.
5. A page whose policy denies the current actor renders its permission-denied state and the shell offers the page's declared recovery target.

## Requirement 7: Stable addressing and affordance sidecar

**User Story:** As an agent driving a browser, I want to find every control by meaning and read what a page offers so that I never guess from pixels.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every action control renders data-rex=<page>/<action>, every region landmark renders data-rex-region=<page>/<region>, every overlay renders data-rex-overlay=<page>/<overlay>, the page root renders data-rex-page=<page>.
2. Addresses are derived from declaration names and are identical across builds and style changes.
3. Each rendered page contains exactly one script element with type application/rex+json and id rex-page whose payload matches the shape in [design] sidecar and validates against the published JSON schema.
4. The sidecar payload updates within one render of any change to data state, action availability, overlay open state or outcome, and window.__rex holds the same object.
5. Every action listed in the sidecar has a visible control in the DOM with a matching data-rex address while the action is available; the checker and the operability walk both report a mismatch.

## Requirement 8: Four invocation routes

**User Story:** As an agent, I want every action reachable by click, keyboard, URL and command palette so that I can choose the cheapest route.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every action declared on a page is reachable by clicking its control, by its declared shortcut, by the URL act parameter and by selecting it in the palette.
2. The palette opens with mod+k, lists the active page's actions and all navigable pages from the manifest, filters by label and id, and executes or navigates on enter.
3. A disallowed action appears in the palette and sidecar as not allowed with the policy reason; it does not execute.

## Requirement 9: Density and motion preference

**User Story:** As an agent or a user with accessibility needs, I want a flat, still, fully expanded layout on request without a separate UI.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The density preference is resolved from the density query parameter, then the x-rex-density header, then the stored preference, then default.
2. Agent density sets data-rex-density=agent on the root, which disables non-essential motion, expands collapsed groups, and enlarges hit targets to at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels through tokens.
3. No state is conveyed only by color or motion; the checker reports a motion-only state change where detectable, and the demo passes a manual audit.

## Requirement 10: No agent traps

**User Story:** As an agent, I want no control that requires hovering, dragging or a canvas so that I can always complete a task.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The checker reports an onMouseEnter or onMouseOver handler without a matching onFocus handler, a draggable element without a declared keyboard alternative, and a canvas element without a declared equivalent action.
2. Every overlay declares its dismissal; Escape and the declared dismiss control both close it; focus returns to the opener.
3. Every date, token or entity picker accepts typed input in addition to selection.
4. Every list that loads more on scroll also exposes a paged route with page and size params.

## Requirement 11: Generated manifest

**User Story:** As Codify or Gideon, I want one machine-readable file describing the app so that I never crawl the source.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. rex manifest writes .rex/manifest.json containing every entity, action, page (with regions, overlays, states, chrome, route), policy and flow with deterministic key ordering.
2. rex manifest writes AGENTS.md from the manifest with the page table, action table and the folder convention; a hand-edited AGENTS.md is overwritten and the checker warns when it is stale.
3. The server serves the same manifest at GET /rex/manifest and the client reads it at startup.

## Requirement 12: The checker

**User Story:** As an agent, I want one command whose structured failures tell me exactly what to fix so that red to green is mechanical.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. rex check runs typecheck, boundaries, states, parity, naming, traps and manifest freshness and exits 1 on any error finding.
2. rex check --json emits an array of findings with rule, severity, file, line, column, message and hint; the human format prints the same findings grouped by file.
3. Each rule is individually testable against fixture directories and has at least one passing and one failing fixture.
4. rex check completes on the demo app in under 30 seconds on the reference machine.

## Requirement 13: Generators

**User Story:** As an agent, I want skeletons written by the tool so that I only fill in handler bodies and parts.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. rex new <name> writes a complete app that passes rex check with zero findings.
2. rex make page <id> --regions a,b --overlays X,Y writes page.ts, view.tsx, states.tsx with all nine exports, hooks/, regions/a/region.tsx, regions/b/region.tsx, overlays/X.tsx, overlays/Y.tsx and test/; the result passes rex check.
3. rex make action|entity|policy|flow|region|part|overlay write the canonical skeleton at the conventional path and refuse to overwrite an existing file.
4. rex promote <page>/regions/<region>/parts/<Part> moves the part to app/components and rewrites imports in the source page.

## Requirement 14: Dev, build and single deployable

**User Story:** As a developer, I want one command to run the whole app and one artifact to deploy.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. rex dev starts one process serving the Vite client and the Hono server on one port with hot reload.
2. rex build emits one directory containing the server entry and the client assets; node dist/server.js serves the app.
3. rex dev and rex build fail fast with the checker's findings when rex check reports errors, unless --no-check is passed.

## Requirement 15: Policy evaluation

**User Story:** As an operator, I want one permission table consulted by the server, the UI and the sidecar so that gating never disagrees.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. policy() declares named permissions and a resolver from actor to granted permissions; requires() and can() build policy predicates.
2. The server evaluates the action's policy before the handler and returns FORBIDDEN with the reason when denied; the handler does not run.
3. The client evaluates the same policy against the current actor to set allowed in the sidecar and disable controls, and the server result is authoritative on disagreement.

## Requirement 16: Audit ledger

**User Story:** As an operator, I want every action invocation recorded so that agent activity is reviewable.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The ledger interface exposes append and list with filters by actor, action id, outcome and time range; an in-memory implementation ships.
2. Records contain actor, action id, input digest (sha-256 of canonical JSON), outcome ok or error code, effect class, duration and timestamp; raw input is not stored.
3. A handler failure still writes a record with the error code.

## Requirement 17: Flow primitive

**User Story:** As an agent harness, I want durable multi-step work with approval gates so that long tasks survive restarts and humans can sign off.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. flow() declares ordered steps, each an action or an approval gate, with a journal adapter; an in-memory journal ships.
2. A flow instance records each completed step; resuming an instance continues from the first incomplete step.
3. An approval gate pauses the flow, exposes an approve and reject action in the sidecar of the owning page, and resumes or terminates on decision.

## Requirement 18: Operability walk

**User Story:** As a release engineer, I want proof that an agent can operate every page so that the contract is tested, not asserted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A Playwright script reads /rex/manifest, visits every page, and for every declared action verifies reachability by click, keyboard, URL and palette.
2. The walk verifies that the sidecar lists exactly the actions whose controls are present, that every overlay declared is dismissible, and that the outcome region updates after each invocation.
3. The walk emits a JSON report per page and exits 1 on any failure.

## Requirement 19: Demo application

**User Story:** As the Rex team, I want a realistic app built only with the convention so that every rule is exercised.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The demo declares at least two entities (account, token), four actions (send, pick token, pick contact, toggle hide dust), two policies and two pages (portfolio, send) with regions, overlays, hooks and all nine states.
2. The demo passes rex check with zero findings and the operability walk with zero failures.
3. The demo is generated with rex new and rex make and then filled in; no file deviates from the skeleton layout.

## Requirement 20: Design tokens and components

**User Story:** As a designer, I want every visual value to come from tokens so that generated UI stays on-system.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. app/components holds DesignX UI copies; parts import only from app/components and the Rex layout primitives.
2. The checker reports raw color classes, arbitrary values and inline style colors outside token references.
3. Rex layout primitives Page.Stack, Page.Grid, Page.Section and Page.Outcome accept only token-based spacing props.

## Requirement 21: Entity storage

**User Story:** As an app author, I want an entity to carry its schema and storage so that CRUD needs no hand-written glue.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. entity() derives the TypeScript type, zod validator and JSON schema from one field definition.
2. The store adapter interface exposes get, list with filter and paging, put and delete; the in-memory adapter passes the adapter conformance test.
3. The Drizzle adapter passes the same conformance test against libsql.

## Requirement 22: Overlays

**User Story:** As an agent, I want every sheet and dialog declared, addressable and dismissible so that I am never trapped.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. overlay() wraps a component with id, declared dismiss behavior and open state bound to region state or URL.
2. Open overlays appear in the sidecar with open true and the dismiss method; closed overlays appear with open false.
3. An overlay traps focus while open, restores focus on close and renders data-rex-overlay.
